summary:
A 3D survival game where a student wakes up alone on Mars after a rocket explosion, reaches the base before oxygen runs out, and survives 30 sols by solving STEM tasks in math, biology, chemistry and engineering.
Full description
After an explosion during liftoff from Mars, the hero wakes up in a spacesuit among burning wreckage. A warning says “Oxygen shortage”. The player must find the damaged base and get inside. Then the player must survive 30 sols until a rescue crew arrives. Oxygen and food drop every sol, radiation grows, solar flares come with a one-sol warning, and dust storms cut power.

The player earns ⭐ points by reading short NASA learning cards and solving STEM missions on the base wall screen: assembling repair parts (engineering), calculating dose, power and oxygen (math), and planting and watering crops (biology). Points are spent on repairs, oxygen, food and radiation shielding. The goal is to make real mission trade-offs tangible and fun, and to inspire young people to study science and space.
How NASA data and resources were used
The game is based on public NASA information: radiation measured on Mars by Curiosity (RAD), the 2018 dust storm that ended the Opportunity rover’s mission, oxygen production from CO₂ by MOXIE on Perseverance, solar-flare warnings in DONKI, and space-radiation biology in OSDR. The flare scenarios are simplified and inspired by real events. The game does not call NASA APIs live yet; importing real DONKI event data is our next step
